Signature feature · @sawah/hieroglyphs
Your name, written in hieroglyphs
Arabic or Latin input mapped to one-sound signs from a 1,072-sign catalogue machine-verified against Unicode.
Honest by design: shown as a phonetic approximation, never a “translation”.
Sign-by-sign breakdown — Gardiner code, what each sign depicts, and where Egyptian had no matching sound.
Four cartouche styles, gender determinative, PNG export and share links.

@sawah/calendar · pure TypeScript
The Egyptian year — still running
Two real calendars computed side by side, with the drift between them shown instead of smoothed over. Same day, 12 October 2026:
Coptic calendar · in use today
2 Paopi 1743
٢ بابه ١٧٤٣
Season Akhet — the inundation · month 2 of the season · year began 11 Sep 2026
Ancient civil year · the “wandering” year
29 Meshir 2775
٢٩ أمشير
Era of Nabonassar · no leap day, so it slips a day every 4 years — 218 days away from the Coptic date today
Coptic · day 32
Civil · day 179
Akhet · inundation (4 × 30 days)Peret · emergence (4 × 30)Shemu · harvest (4 × 30)+5 days
365 days, no leap day — the civil year slips ¼ day a year and laps the seasons every ~1,460 years.
The Coptic year keeps the same shape plus the Alexandrian leap day — still used by farmers and the Church.
Epoch named, never faked: the Era of Nabonassar (747 BCE), the astronomers' convention since Ptolemy.
Rendered from the real output of describeToday() / describeCivilToday() for this case study — a data illustration, not an app screenshot.

Arena · @sawah/senet · @sawah/twenty
5,000-year-old board games, playable
Senet and Twenty Squares as pure rules engines — no clock, no randomness of their own; the caller throws the sticks.
Computer at 3 levels; hard = 2-ply expectiminimax weighing every throw.
Play a friend or online, with replays, a lesson and a daily puzzle.
Plus a daily challenge and quiz games over 7,500 questions.

Hieroglyph Academy · @sawah/learning
Learn the script, then keep it
Spaced repetition on the published SM-2 algorithm — not a home-made schedule.
Alphabet cards, a full sign catalogue and a glossary, all with transliteration and meaning.
Playful tools: “Which ancient Egyptian are you?”, wallpapers, and an embeddable sign-of-the-day widget.
